title: Microsoft Dataverse: Python SDK for scripting and agent workflows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, documented SDK operations and general governance controls are supported. It distinguishes package installation from the roadmap's automatic-enablement wording and confines its licensing uncertainty to what the SDK pages publish.

claims.claim: The SDK lets Python developers and data scientists work with Dataverse without .NET knowledge.
claims.quote: You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse by using familiar Python syntax. You don't need any .NET knowledge.

claims.claim: The SDK supports create, retrieve, update and delete data operations.
claims.quote: CRUD operations | Support for create, retrieve, update, and delete data operations by using a single request.

claims.claim: Bulk operations use CreateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: Bulk operations use UpdateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Bulk operations use UpsertMultiple.
claims.quote: A single item uses a PATCH request while multiple items use the UpsertMultiple bulk action.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Bulk operations can remove multiple rows using BulkDelete in a web service call.
claims.quote: Specify multiple operations in a single web service call. This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: The SDK supports read-only direct SQL SELECT queries.
claims.quote: Direct-SQL queries | Supports simple read-only "SELECT" statements with paging.

claims.claim: The SDK provides pandas DataFrame wrappers for CRUD operations.
claims.quote: Client wrappers are provided for all CRUD operations where DataFrames and Series data types are returned to the caller.

claims.claim: The SDK uploads files to Dataverse file columns.
claims.quote: File operations | Upload files to a Dataverse file column with automatic chunking for large files.

claims.claim: The SDK supports batch requests.
claims.quote: Batch operations | Send multiple CRUD, table metadata, and SQL query operations in a single HTTP request with optional transactional changesets.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SDK supports creating, updating and deleting custom tables.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SDK supports creating, updating and deleting custom columns.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns

claims.claim: The SDK provides structured error handling.
claims.quote: Error handling: structured exception hierarchy with detailed error context and retry guidance.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging is opt-in and writes all HTTP requests and responses to a file.
claims.quote: HTTP diagnostics logging: opt-in file-based logging of all HTTP requests and responses

claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging redacts sensitive headers such as authorization.
claims.quote: with automatic redaction of sensitive headers, such as authorization.

claims.claim: The SDK internally calls the Dataverse Web API.
claims.quote: The SDK provides a Python programming interface that internally calls the Dataverse Web API.

claims.claim: The SDK authenticates using Azure Identity credentials.
claims.quote: The SDK client requires any Azure Identity TokenCredential implementation for OAuth authentication with Dataverse.

claims.claim: pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client installs the SDK from PyPI.
claims.quote:
This command installs the latest stable release of the SDK from a pypi.org package.

```bash
pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client
```

claims.claim: Getting started specifies Python 3.10+.
claims.quote: An activated Python 3.10+ environment.

claims.claim: The reference architecture specifies Python 3.13 or later, differing from Getting started.
claims.quote: Python 3.13 or later

claims.claim: The SDK overview feature list does not name autonomous data agents, form prediction, autofill, MCP or A2A.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse SDK for Python" disable admin; licensing pricing meter. Read the complete SDK overview feature list, including authentication, data operations, metadata, logging and licensing; it does not name these roadmap capabilities.

claims.claim: The SDK is an interface to existing Dataverse data and security rather than a new datastore or separate permissions model.
claims.quote: Access to data in your Dataverse environment is limited based on the security role (or roles) that an administrator assigns to you, and the data management permissions of that role.

claims.claim: SDK workflows can extract tables into pandas DataFrames for analysis.
claims.quote: Extract and transform: Load tables into Pandas DataFrames for cleaning, feature engineering, and exploratory analysis.

claims.claim: Extracted data is no longer protected by the Dataverse security boundary and must be governed by the customer.
claims.quote: However, after the data has been extracted it is no longer protected by the security boundary provided by Dynamics 365 (online) and is instead controlled directly by the customer.

claims.claim: Getting started shows InteractiveBrowserCredential and AzureCliCredential as development options.
claims.quote:
# Development options
credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication
# credential = AzureCliCredential()          # If logged in via 'az login'

claims.claim: Getting started shows ClientSecretCredential and CertificateCredential as production options.
claims.quote:
# Production options  
# credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)
# credential = CertificateCredential(tenant_id, client_id, cert_path)

claims.claim: General app access control allows or blocks client apps by their application ID.
claims.quote: Dataverse authentication validates the client app ID in the user's token against a list of allowed and blocked apps configured for the environment.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: The app access control prerequisites name Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 admin roles.
claims.quote:
There are two Power Platform related service admin roles you can assign to provide a high level of admin management:
- Power Platform admin
- Dynamics 365 admin

claims.claim: App access control does not apply to partner apps making service-to-service calls.
claims.quote:
Client app access control isn't applied to the following apps:
- First-party apps with service-to-service calls (application context)
- Partner apps with service-to-service calls

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The SDK's authentication context depends on the Azure Identity credential supplied to its client.
claims.quote: client = DataverseClient("https://myorg.crm.dynamics.com", credential)

claims.claim: InteractiveBrowserCredential accepts a client_id specifying the Entra application.
claims.quote:
client_id | str
Client ID of the Microsoft Entra application that users will sign into.

claims.claim: Without client_id, InteractiveBrowserCredential authenticates to an Azure development application.
claims.quote: If not specified, users will authenticate to an Azure development application, which is not recommended for production scenarios.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: client.files.upload automatically creates a missing file column as a permanent schema change.
claims.quote: If the file column doesn't exist, the SDK creates it automatically. Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table, and the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.claim: Schema changes require privileges to customise the table.
claims.quote: Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises creating file columns in advance in production.
claims.quote: In production environments, create file columns in advance rather than relying on automatic creation.

claims.claim: After package installation, dataverse-install-claude-skill optionally installs Claude skills.
claims.quote:
you can optionally install two Claude Skills when installing the SDK from a package.

```bash
pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client && dataverse-install-claude-skill
```

claims.claim: The optional installation installs two Claude skills.
claims.quote:
The two skills are described in the following list:
- dataverse-sdk-use: Apply best practices for using the SDK in your applications.
- dataverse-sdk-dev: Provide guidance for developing and contributing to the SDK itself.

claims.claim: Installed skill definitions are stored on the developer's computer.
claims.quote: Once installed, you can find skill definitions in the .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-use/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-dev/SKILL.md files on your development computer.

claims.claim: The SDK automatically retries temporary failures such as API throttling.
claims.quote: Automatic retries | Handle networking problems that might occur for operations that fail due to temporary problems, such as API throttling or service unavailability.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits apply to external web service requests, including SDK traffic.
claims.quote: Service protection limits apply to all external web service requests, not only the CRUD operations on tables counted against entitlement limits.

claims.claim: Heavy scripts can affect other callers sharing a user account because service protection limits include per-account constraints.
claims.quote: We limit the number of concurrent connections per user account, the number of API requests per connection, and the amount of execution time that can be used for each connection.

claims.claim: Dataverse CRUD, assign and share operations count toward request limits regardless of client or SOAP/REST endpoint.
claims.quote: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations including user-driven and internal system requests required to complete CRUD transactions

claims.claim: Application, non-interactive, administrative and system identities use pooled tenant-level request limits.
claims.quote: These limits are defined and pooled at the tenant level. Dataverse enables you to have identities that don't require any user to interact with the service. These identities include:

claims.claim: Writing rows or files can consume Dataverse storage capacity.
claims.quote: you see your storage capacity entitlement and usage by database, file, and log as it appears in the Microsoft Power Platform admin center today.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents installation from the GitHub source repository as an alternative to PyPI.
claims.quote: Run the following command to install the SDK from the project's GitHub source instead of from the package. Install the client from the PyPi package or from the source, but not both.

claims.claim: App access control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control.
claims.quote: select Security. ... select Identity and access. ... select App access control ... Select the environment ... Select the Set up app access control button. ... in the Access control dropdown list.

claims.claim: pac env list-settings --environment <environment-url> --filter application reads matching organization settings rather than changing app access control.
claims.quote:
pac env list-settings
List environment settings
... --environment ... The value may be a Guid or absolute https URL. ... --filter ... Show only settings containing filter criteria

claims.claim: New application users are reached at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... select Environments. Then select an environment. ... Select Settings. ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Application users. ... Select + New app user

claims.claim: POST to the documented BAP addAppUser endpoint with api-version=2020-10-01 and servicePrincipalAppId creates an environment application user.
claims.quote:
POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01
... "servicePrincipalAppId": "AzureAD_App_Registration_ClientID"

claims.claim: The create-application-user API documentation is marked preview.
claims.quote:
# Create a Dataverse application user (preview)
[This article is pre-release documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The addAppUser API always adds the application user as System Administrator.
claims.quote: This always adds the application user as a System Administrator.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote: select Security > Compliance. ... Select the Auditing tile. ... Select the environment ... Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations with the four listed $select properties reads auditing settings.
claims.quote:
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Changing auditing settings requires System Administrator or System Customizer privileges.
claims.quote: Anyone can view the configuration, but you must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role to change the settings.

claims.claim: Recording scripted data changes requires auditing enabled for the environment, table and column.
claims.quote: First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.claim: User-access logging requires Log access in addition to environment auditing.
claims.quote: To turn on user access auditing (log access) or activity logging (Read logs), turn on auditing at the environment level.

claims.claim: App access control offers audit mode for reviewing apps before enabling enforcement.
claims.quote: app access control isn't enforced in audit mode. You get a list of apps accessing the environment whether or not they're allowed or denied access.

claims.claim: The audit log contains ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed events for app access control.
claims.quote: Select the dropdown arrow near the Event heading, then find and select ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed.

claims.claim: Microsoft points to deactivating or deleting environment application users to block partner service-to-service apps.
claims.quote:
Partner apps with service-to-service calls

To block these apps, make them inactive or delete them from the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Security roles for people can be assigned through the environment's Users + permissions settings.
claims.quote: Select Users + permissions > Security roles. ... Select Members ... select the + Add people. ... enter a name, email address, or team name ... Select Add

claims.claim: The SDK Learn setup pages describe installation rather than the roadmap's automatic-enablement wording.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse SDK for Python" disable admin. Opened overview, get-started, quick-guide, work-data and architecture. Setup says to install the SDK and establish a client connection; none states automatic enablement for admins/makers/marketers.
